title: Barista Salary: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay (2026–27 Tax Guide)
description: Calculate your barista salary from hourly rate using 38-hour week. Includes award rates, casual loading, super, and tax for 2026–27.
salarySummary: For a full-time barista on the Hospitality Award Level 1 rate of $26.44 per hour, the annual gross salary is approximately $52,254 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a barista in Australia?
faqs.a: Under the Hospitality Industry (General) Award 2020, a barista is typically classified as a Food and beverage attendant. From 1 July 2026, the minimum hourly rate for Level 1 is $26.44, and for Level 2 it is $27.08. These rates apply to full-time and part-time employees. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, bringing the casual rate to $33.05 per hour for Level 1.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to a barista's pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the ordinary hourly rate as compensation for not receiving paid leave entitlements. For a barista on the Level 1 rate of $26.44, the casual rate becomes $33.05 per hour. When calculating annual salary, you should apply the loading to the hourly rate before multiplying by hours and weeks. Our [timesheet](/) includes a checkbox to add casual loading automatically.

faqs.q: How does tax affect my barista salary?
faqs.a: Your barista salary is subject to progressive tax rates and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the tax-free threshold is $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide to estimate your net pay after tax and super.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Barista Salary from Your Hourly Rate

If you work as a barista or are considering a role in hospitality, you may want to know what your hourly rate means in annual terms. A **barista salary** is most commonly calculated from an hourly wage under the Hospitality Industry (General) Award 2020, which sets minimum rates for food and beverage attendants. The standard full-time week is 38 hours, and the annual gross figure is simply your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours and then by 52 weeks.

For example, a barista at the award’s Level 1 rate of $26.44 per hour earns approximately $52,254 per year before tax and super. If you are casual, the 25% loading brings the hourly rate to $33.05, giving an annual gross of about $65,318. These figures assume you work every week of the year with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

### The Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

The core conversion is straightforward:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time barista on 38 hours: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.40. If you work part-time, use your actual weekly hours. The same formula works for any hourly rate. You can also calculate your fortnightly pay by doubling the weekly amount. For the Level 1 barista, the weekly minimum is $1,004.90, so the fortnight is $2,009.80.

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It then shows your annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay. It also estimates tax and super, so you can see your take-home pay.

## Award Rates and the National Minimum Wage

The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) that list the minimum rates for each award. For baristas, the relevant award is the Hospitality Industry (General) Award 2020. As of 1 July 2026, the minimum rates are:

- Introductory level: $25.74 per hour ($978.10 per week)
- Level 1 (Food and beverage attendant grade 1): $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week)
- Level 2 (Food and beverage attendant grade 2): $27.08 per hour ($1,029.10 per week)

Most experienced baristas will be classified at Level 1 or Level 2. The National Minimum Wage is also $26.44 per hour, so the award rate matches the minimum. However, some employers may pay above the award, especially for skilled baristas in busy cafes.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees under the award receive a 25% loading on top of the ordinary hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid sick leave, annual leave, or public holiday pay. For a Level 1 barista, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour. When calculating your barista salary as a casual, always apply the loading to the base rate before multiplying by hours. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains this in more detail.

## Superannuation and Tax on Your Barista Salary

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross salary. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a barista earning $52,254, the employer must contribute an additional $6,270.48 into your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra benefit.

### Tax Brackets 2026–27

Your barista salary is taxed using the resident tax scales. For 2026–27:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (generally). For a full-time barista on $52,254, the tax would be approximately $7,567 plus the Medicare levy of $1,045, leaving a net annual income of around $43,642. This is an estimate and does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

You can use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool to get a more precise estimate based on your circumstances.

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) is designed for exactly this conversion. You enter your base hourly rate – for example, $26.44 for a Level 1 barista. If you are casual, tick the box to add 25% casual loading. The calculator then shows your annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay. It also applies the 2026–27 tax rates and Medicare levy to estimate your net pay, and adds the 12% super contribution on top.

Remember, the result assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It also assumes you are a resident for tax purposes and claim the full tax-free threshold. For award-specific allowances or penalty rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Why 38 Hours?

The 38-hour week is the standard full-time ordinary hours under most awards, including the Hospitality Award. Part-time and casual hours vary, so adjust the weekly hours in the formula accordingly. The [reference tables](/data) on our site list the standard hours for different industries.

## Final Thoughts on Your Barista Salary

Knowing your annual barista salary helps you compare job offers, budget, and plan for tax time. The formula is simple, but the details matter – casual loading, super, and tax brackets all affect your real income. Use the Fair Work Ombudsman’s award rates as a baseline, and check your pay slip to ensure you are receiving the correct entitlements.

For a quick calculation, head to our [timesheet](/) and enter your hourly rate. It does the maths for you, including the 25% casual loading if applicable. Whether you are a full-time barista or working casual shifts, understanding your annual pay puts you in control.
